User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the NEU Library Visitor Log system, storing their institutional details and system status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The institutional email address of the user, used for authentication and identification.

firstName.description: The first name of the user, typically obtained from the authentication system.

lastName.description: The last name of the user, typically obtained from the authentication system.

affiliation.description: The user's college or office affiliation, captured during their first visit to the library.

role.description: The role of the user within the system, such as 'user' or 'admin'.

isBlocked.description: A flag indicating whether the user has been blocked by an administrator from accessing the library system.

createdAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the user's account was first created in the system.

lastLoginAt.description: The timestamp of the user's most recent successful login.

VisitPurpose.title: VisitPurpose
VisitPurpose.description: Defines a standardized reason or purpose for visiting the NEU Library, available for users to select.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VisitPurpose entity.

name.description: The short, displayable name of the visit purpose (e.g., 'Reading', 'Research', 'Computer Use', 'Studying').

description.description: A more detailed description of the visit purpose.

Visit.title: Visit
Visit.description: Logs a single instance of a user checking into the NEU Library, including their purposes and check-in/out times.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Visit entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made this visit. (Relationship: User 1:N Visit)

checkInTime.description: The timestamp marking when the user checked into the library.

checkOutTime.description: The timestamp marking when the user checked out of the library. This field can be null if the user is still present or if check-out is not recorded.

purposeIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the VisitPurpose entities that describe the user's reason(s) for the visit. (Relationship: VisitPurpose N:N Visit)

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The document ID (`userId`) must match the Firebase Authentication UID. Includes denormalized 'role' and 'isBlocked' fields for authorization. Admins can manage these documents.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user.

definition.description: Stores individual visit logs for a specific user. 'userId' is part of the path, ensuring strong ownership and authorization independence for each visit document. Users can manage their own visits, while admins can view all visits via collection group queries.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the user who made the visit.

params.name: visitId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific library visit.

definition.description: Stores predefined reasons for visiting the library. This collection is globally readable by all authenticated users for selection in the UI. Writable only by administrators.

params.name: purposeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific visit purpose.

definition.description: A dedicated collection to store UIDs of users who have administrator privileges. Used for quick existence checks in security rules (`exists(...)`) to grant admin access. Documents in this collection only need to contain the UID as the document ID; the content is often minimal or empty.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of an administrator.

definition.description: A singleton document storing aggregated daily visitor count and other relevant statistics. Globally readable for display on dashboards, writable only by trusted backend processes (e.g., Cloud Functions).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation to ensure secure, scalable, and easily debuggable security rules. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**

1.  **User Data and Visits:** For `/users/{userId}` and `/users/{userId}/visits/{visitId}`, authorization relies directly on `request.auth.uid` matching the `{userId}` wildcard in the path. This means that a user's own data and their visits are inherently owned by them based on the document path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to a parent document to determine ownership. Each visit document `/users/{userId}/visits/{visitId}` contains its `userId` field, reinforcing ownership and making subcollection authorization atomic and independent of the parent `user` document's attributes. This directly addresses the mandate to denormalize authorization context where a subcollection's access depends on parent attributes.
2.  **Admin Roles:** Administrator status is determined by the existence of a document in the `/roles_admin/{adminId}` collection, where `{adminId}` is the user's `uid`. This uses the 'Existence over Content' principle, allowing a simple `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` check in security rules, which is highly efficient, atomic, and authorization independent.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

1.  **User-Specific Data:** The `/users/{userId}/visits/{visitId}` structure allows for efficient `list` operations for a specific user. A user can query their own visits, and the rules can strictly enforce `request.auth.uid == userId`, ensuring only their data is returned. For administrators, a Collection Group Query on `visits` (if enabled) or iterating through users would allow global access to all visit records while still adhering to QAPs, as the query would be fully constrained by server-side rules.
2.  **Global Reference Data:** The `/visit_purposes` collection is designed for global read access by all authenticated users, allowing them to `list` available visit purposes. This collection holds predefined, static data that all users need to see, ensuring that `list` operations are secure and return only relevant, public data.
3.  **Admin-Managed Data:** The `/users` collection allows administrators to `list` all users for management and search functionality, where the rules would grant access based on the `roles_admin` existence check. This supports admin-level `list` operations without relying on filtering sensitive data client-side.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** Primarily private for write operations by the owner, with admin override for management (e.g., blocking users).
*   **User Visits (`/users/{userId}/visits/{visitId}`):** Strongly owned by the user for write operations, with admin read access for statistics.
*   **Global Reference Data (`/visit_purposes/{purposeId}`):** Read-only for all authenticated users; writeable by admins only.
*   **Admin Role Definition (`/roles_admin/{adminId}`):** A dedicated collection for identifying administrators, ensuring a clear and simple security posture for admin checks.
*   **Global Statistics (`/statistics/daily_visitor_count`):** A single document, globally readable, and writable only by trusted backend processes (e.g., Cloud Functions).

This structure ensures that each collection and subcollection has a consistent security posture, simplifying rule writing and minimizing complexity.
